svg.text: Chatham AI Advisory hosting platform on Azure: multi-client solution architecture
One subscription per client (ADR 0001), built from the same Terraform stamp, inside Platform Engineering's landing zone. Every client resource below is private; nothing is shared between clients.
Entra ID tenant and governance (owned by Platform Engineering / P&T)
ADR 0002: AI Advisory is a landing-zone consumer. P&T owns hierarchy, policy, identity and connectivity; we build inside their guardrails.
Subscription vending: P&T template per client (MG placement, IPAM /22, Entra groups, budget owner, AOAI quota request)
Azure Policy add-on (Gatekeeper) enforces the same initiatives inside every AKS cluster. Exemptions are time-boxed and recorded in an ADR.

Apply identities: Contributor + RBAC Administrator limited by an ABAC condition to KV Secrets User, OpenAI User, Blob Data Contributor/Reader, Search Index Reader, Metrics Publisher, Reader, Network Contributor, Private DNS Zone Contributor, Managed Identity Operator, AKS RBAC Reader, Cognitive Services User (and AcrPull on the shared ACR only).
AI Advisory shared platform (no client data)
Per client: client data, nothing shared
Private routed path: client network -> ExpressRoute/VPN gateway -> hub firewall (one rule per client) -> App Gateway WAF
Public user path (opt-in): internet -> App Gateway public IP, NSG + WAF allow-list
Model path: app -> AI gateway (Entra token) -> Azure OpenAI private endpoint (gateway MI)
Egress: every spoke workload subnet -> hub firewall (UDR); spoke-to-spoke denied
Private Link path: client's own Azure VNet -> private endpoint -> App Gateway Private Link (no hub routing)

Sources: docs/adr/0001-0013, terraform/stamps/client, terraform/modules/hub-connectivity, terraform/platform, terraform/clients/*. Addresses and names are the example configs; every value comes from a client's ~40-line tfvars.
